paymentIntro: Three Ways You Can Pay for Reputation Management

Reputation management services pricing isn't a single price list — there are three payment models, and which one applies depends on whether the work is ongoing, finite, or urgent. Most reputation management fees fall into one of these three billing shapes, whatever provider you use, so it helps to know which one you're actually buying.

paymentModels.label: Most common
paymentModels.title: Retainer
paymentModels.description: Billed monthly, scoped to an agreed KPI cycle — reviewed and reset every quarter. The default model for ongoing coverage.
paymentModels.usage: Used for: RH Detection, RH Control, RH Personal.

paymentModels.label: Finite scope
paymentModels.title: Project
paymentModels.description: A fixed deliverable, fixed fee, fixed timeline — no recurring billing. Used where there's a clear finish line.
paymentModels.usage: Used for: Risk Check diagnostics, negative content removal, pre-deal and pre-IPO profile preparation.

paymentModels.label: Active crisis
paymentModels.title: Project + Urgency Premium
paymentModels.description: Priced as a project because the engagement is time-boxed by the crisis itself, with a premium for 24/7 priority response.
paymentModels.usage: Used for: RH Defence, acute RH Personal Crisis response.

marketIntro: Reputation Management Costs: The Price of Finding Out Late
Two patterns from 2026 that inform how this is priced — not case studies of our work, but the market data the pricing logic above is built on.

marketCases.title: Wix, Intuit and Medpace
marketCases.label: Narrative gap
marketCases.description: Thirteen securities-fraud investigations opened in thirteen consecutive weeks in 2026, all following the same mechanism: a public narrative diverges from operating reality, and the market reprices the stock in a single session once it finds out. Wix (−27%), Intuit (−20%) and Medpace (−15.9%) are among the recent examples.

marketCases.title: KPMG Australia
marketCases.label: Governance
marketCases.description: At KPMG Australia, a mishandled whistleblower complaint cost the CEO and the head of audit their jobs on the same day. Within two weeks the regulator had opened an investigation into three partners, and government contracts were at risk — the exposure widened in scope, not just severity, the longer it went unmanaged.

marketConclusion: Reputation risk is rarely priced by what it is today — it's priced by how fast it escalates once it's public.

That's the return on investment case for reputation management in plain terms: independent research puts intangible assets like brand and reputation at roughly 90% of S&P 500 market value, and separate studies tie a meaningful share of a company's valuation directly to its reputation.

faq.title: How much does digital reputation protection cost?
faq.answer: RH Detection starts at $5,000/month, RH Control from $10,000/month per region, RH Defence from $50,000/month in an active crisis, and RH Personal from $5,000/month. Inside each, the exact price depends on the KPIs and timeline you agree to — see the full menu by solution above.

faq.title: Why does the price depend on KPIs, not just a package?
faq.answer: Because scope of work is set to hit an agreed target, not a generic task list. Once we agree what "done" looks like — coverage, SLA, share of voice — the work and the price that gets you there follow directly, not the other way around.

faq.title: Why is this a monthly retainer instead of a one-time project?
faq.answer: Because the risk is continuous. New content, reviews and AI answers appear every week — a one-time fix doesn't stop the field from producing risk again. RH Defence and acute RH Personal crisis work are priced as projects instead, since they're time-boxed by nature.

faq.title: Can we finish faster, for more per month?
faq.answer: Yes — the same KPI can usually be hit in 6 months or 12. Compressing the timeline concentrates more work into each month, which raises the monthly rate; spreading it out lowers the monthly rate and extends the commitment. The end state is generally the same either way.

faq.title: Can we start with a smaller budget?
faq.answer: Yes — start with Risk Check, a free, affordable reputation management diagnostic across search, AI, reviews and media. It shows exactly where the exposure is, so the first paid engagement is scoped to what needs protecting, not a guess.

faq.title: We're in a crisis right now. What happens?
faq.answer: RH Defence starts immediately, not after a standard sales cycle. It's priced as a project with an urgency premium rather than a retainer, because the engagement is time-boxed to containing the active phase.

faq.title: Do you guarantee results or removal?
faq.answer: No. Search algorithms, AI models and GDPR rules limit what any provider can guarantee. We don't promise removal or a fixed ranking outcome — we commit to continuous, expert-led management of the risk, which is a different promise.

faq.title: Is reputation management worth the cost?
faq.answer: Usually, yes, for the buyers this is built for. Research on CEO reputation has tied a significant share of a company's market value to how its leadership is perceived, and separate research on Yelp ratings found that a one-star swing in a business's rating measurably moves revenue. Reputation management isn't priced against zero — it's priced against what a damaged search result, review pattern or AI answer would have cost you in a lost deal, a stalled raise or a hire who walked away.

faq.title: How much does reputation management cost?

The exact number follows from the KPIs and timeline you agree to, not a seat count or a package tier.
